title: Medieval History Lec 2
summary: Vijayanagara was founded by Harihara and Bukka in 1336; capital Hampi (named after Goddess Pampa) on the banks of the Tungabhadra; the Hampi stone chariot appears on the ₹50 note.
Dynasties of Vijayanagara: Sangama (1336-1485), Saluva (1485-1505), Tuluva (1505-1570), Aravidu (1570-1650); Battle of Talikota in 1565.
Titles: Vijayanagara rulers - Narapati, Deccan Sultans - Ashvapati, Odisha rulers - Gajapati; Vijayanagara rulers called themselves 'Hindu Suratrana'.
Krishnadeva Raya: 'Andhra Bhoja'; wrote Amuktamalyada (Telugu) and Jambavati Kalyanam (Sanskrit); Ashtadiggajas at his court (Tenali Rama, Peddana, Mallana etc.); Amara-nayaka system.
The Bahmani kingdom was founded in 1347 by Alauddin Bahman Shah; its southern boundary was the Krishna; the Raichur Doab lies between the Krishna and the Tungabhadra.
Five successor states of the Bahmani kingdom: Berar - Imad Shahi, Bijapur - Adil Shahi (Gol Gumbaz), Ahmadnagar - Nizam Shahi, Bidar - Barid Shahi, Golconda - Qutb Shahi (Charminar).
Babur: descendant of Timur and Genghis Khan; Panipat 1526, Khanwa 1527, Chanderi 1528, Ghaghra 1529, died 1530; Tuzuk-i-Baburi written in Turki, translated into Persian by Abdur Rahim Khan-i-Khanan.

Humayun: defeated by Sher Shah at Chausa (1539) and Bilgram/Kannauj (1540); took refuge with the Safavids of Iran; returned in 1555 and died in 1556 after falling from the stairs; Humayun-nama by Gulbadan Begum.
Sher Shah: sarkar = shiq, pargana, suba; muqaddam, fotedar; died at Kalinjar in 1545; tomb at Sasaram; Akbar adopted his administrative system.
Akbar: ascended the throne at 13; Second Battle of Panipat 1556 (Bairam Khan vs Hemu); Sulh-i-Kul; Mansabdari 1571; Din-i-Ilahi 1582; Dahsala/Zabti 1580 (Todar Mal: Polaj, Parauti, Chachar, Banjar).
Mughal posts: Mir Bakhshi (military), Mir Saman (karkhanas), Sadr-us-Sudur (religious affairs), Diwan (revenue), Subedar (province); Akbarnama has 3 volumes, the third is the Ain-i-Akbari.
Aurangzeb (1658-1707): took the title Alamgir; annexed Bijapur (1686) and Golconda (1687); Lachit Borphukan won the Battle of Saraighat in 1671 (NDA gold medal named after him).
Independent states: Awadh - Burhan-ul-Mulk, Hyderabad - Asaf Jah, Bengal - Murshid Quli Khan; Nadir Shah's invasion of 1739 (Karnal, Peacock Throne, Muhammad Shah 'Rangila').

Mughal architecture: arches and domes; Fatehpur Sikri (1571), Buland Darwaza (c. 1575, conquest of Gujarat); Taj Mahal (1631-53, Ustad Ahmad Lahori); pietra dura first seen at Itmad-ud-Daulah's tomb; Humayun's Tomb in charbagh style; Bibi ka Maqbara is the 'Taj of the Deccan'.

Third Battle of Panipat 1761 (Abdali vs Sadashivrao Bhau; aided by Najib-ud-Daulah and Shuja-ud-Daulah); Anglo-Maratha wars: Salbai 1782, Bassein 1802, Pindari War 1817-18, Peshwa Baji Rao II sent to Bithur.

mcqs.q: After the fall of Kampili (c. 1327), Harihara and Bukka are believed to have been taken captive to Delhi during the reign of which Sultan?
mcqs.e: Muhammad bin Tughlaq ruled 1325-1351; the brothers later founded Vijayanagara on the Tungabhadra.

mcqs.q: Which two brothers founded the Vijayanagara Empire?
o: Deva Raya I and Deva Raya II
mcqs.e: The Sangama brothers Harihara and Bukka founded Vijayanagara in 1336.

mcqs.q: The Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi mentions which Sultan appointing low-born persons to high administrative posts?
mcqs.e: Barani criticised this policy of Muhammad bin Tughlaq in the Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi.

mcqs.q: Muhammad bin Tughlaq shifted his capital from Delhi to which place?
mcqs.e: The transfer failed and the capital was later moved back to Delhi.

mcqs.q: Which of the following schemes of Muhammad bin Tughlaq failed?
mcqs.e: He issued token coins of copper and brass, which failed due to large-scale forgery.

mcqs.q: What was the name of the agriculture department set up by Muhammad bin Tughlaq?
mcqs.e: Diwan-i-Amir-i-Kohi (Diwan-i-Kohi) was his department of agriculture.

mcqs.q: What were the agricultural loans given to peasants by Muhammad bin Tughlaq called?
mcqs.e: Sondhar/taccavi loans were a key part of his agrarian reforms.

mcqs.q: Which was the first dynasty of the Vijayanagara Empire?
mcqs.e: Order: Sangama, Saluva, Tuluva, Aravidu.

mcqs.q: The Sangama dynasty ruled approximately during which period?
mcqs.e: The Sangama dynasty ruled from 1336 to 1485.

mcqs.q: Who founded the Saluva dynasty?
mcqs.e: The Saluva dynasty ruled roughly from 1485 to 1505.

mcqs.q: Who founded the Tuluva dynasty?
mcqs.e: The Tuluva dynasty ruled c. 1505-1570; Krishnadeva Raya belonged to it.

mcqs.q: Who founded the Aravidu dynasty, the fourth and last dynasty of Vijayanagara?
mcqs.e: The Aravidu dynasty lasted roughly from 1570 to 1650.

mcqs.q: During which period did the Tuluva dynasty of Vijayanagara rule?
mcqs.e: The Tuluva dynasty ruled from 1505 to 1570.

mcqs.q: The Aravidu dynasty ruled approximately during which period?
mcqs.e: Sriranga III of this dynasty is regarded as the last ruler.

mcqs.q: In which century was the Vijayanagara Empire founded?
mcqs.e: Vijayanagara was founded in 1336, i.e. the 14th century.

mcqs.q: Hampi, the capital of the Vijayanagara Empire, is located on the banks of which river?
mcqs.e: Hampi lies on the banks of the Tungabhadra.

mcqs.q: Hampi is believed to be named after which goddess?
mcqs.e: Goddess Pampa is regarded as a form of Parvati.

mcqs.q: Which current Indian currency note depicts the Hampi stone chariot?
mcqs.e: The new ₹50 note carries the image of the stone chariot of Hampi.

mcqs.q: Who brought the ruins of the Vijayanagara Empire to light in 1800?
mcqs.e: Colin Mackenzie, an engineer and antiquarian, later became the first Surveyor General of India.

mcqs.q: What did the rulers of Vijayanagara call themselves?
mcqs.e: 'Hindu Suratrana' (Hindu Sultan) was their title.

mcqs.q: By what name did contemporaries know Vijayanagara?
mcqs.e: Contemporaries referred to it as the 'Karnata Samrajya'.

mcqs.q: What was the title of the rulers of Vijayanagara?
mcqs.e: Narapati - Vijayanagara, Ashvapati - Bahmani/Deccan Sultans, Gajapati - rulers of Odisha.

mcqs.q: What was the title of the rulers of Odisha?
mcqs.e: Gajapati was the title of the rulers of Odisha.

mcqs.q: The Hazara Rama Temple was built during which empire?
mcqs.e: The Hazara Rama Temple, Vitthala Temple and Vijaya Mahal at Hampi belong to the Vijayanagara period.

mcqs.q: The Vitthala Swami Temple at Hampi is dedicated to which deity?
mcqs.e: Vitthala is a form of Vishnu worshipped mainly in Karnataka and Maharashtra.

mcqs.q: The Virupaksha Temple at Hampi is dedicated to which deity?
mcqs.e: Vijayanagara rulers claimed to rule on behalf of Virupaksha, a form of Shiva.

mcqs.q: Who built the Virupaksha Temple at Pattadakal?
mcqs.e: It was built by Lokamahadevi, queen of Chalukya king Vikramaditya II; the Hampi temple is of the Vijayanagara period.

mcqs.q: The Vijayanagara rulers' claim to rule 'on behalf of Virupaksha' resembles which concept?
mcqs.e: Both sought divine legitimacy for kingship; the Kushanas took the title Devaputra.

mcqs.q: When was the Battle of Talikota fought?
mcqs.e: It is also called the Battle of Rakkasa-Tangadi or Bannihatti.

mcqs.q: By what other name is the Battle of Talikota known?
mcqs.e: In it Bijapur, Ahmadnagar and Golconda defeated Vijayanagara.

mcqs.q: Who led Vijayanagara in the Battle of Talikota?
mcqs.e: Rama Raya's defeat led to the decline of Vijayanagara.

mcqs.q: Which states fought against Vijayanagara in the Battle of Talikota?
mcqs.e: States formed after the break-up of the Bahmani kingdom attacked jointly.

mcqs.q: Who is considered the last ruler of Vijayanagara?
mcqs.e: The Aravidu dynasty survived for some time after Talikota; its last ruler was Sriranga III.

mcqs.q: The 'Ashtadiggajas' were poets at whose court?
mcqs.e: Compare the Navaratnas (Chandragupta II/Akbar) and the Ashtapradhan (Shivaji).

mcqs.q: Which of the following was NOT one of Krishnadeva Raya's Ashtadiggajas?
mcqs.e: Abul Fazl was a courtier of Akbar.

mcqs.q: Who wrote 'Rajasekhara Charitra'?
mcqs.e: Madayyagari Mallana was one of the Ashtadiggajas.

mcqs.q: Which is the Telugu work of Krishnadeva Raya?
mcqs.e: He wrote Amuktamalyada in Telugu.

mcqs.q: Which Sanskrit drama was written by Krishnadeva Raya?
mcqs.e: Jambavati Kalyanam is a Sanskrit drama.

mcqs.q: What was the title of Krishnadeva Raya?
mcqs.e: He is known as Andhra Bhoja.

mcqs.q: Who were the 'Amara-nayakas' in Vijayanagara?
mcqs.e: They governed assigned territories and maintained troops; the system resembled the iqta.

mcqs.q: Into which two parts was the city of Vijayanagara divided?
mcqs.e: The Sacred Centre lay to the north and consisted mainly of temples.

mcqs.q: Where is the 'Mahanavami Dibba' located?
mcqs.e: During Mahanavami the Amara-nayakas brought gifts to the king here.

mcqs.q: Who founded the Bahmani kingdom?
mcqs.e: It was founded in 1347 AD.

mcqs.q: When was the Bahmani kingdom founded?
mcqs.e: Eleven years after Vijayanagara.

mcqs.q: Which river formed the southern boundary of the Bahmani kingdom?
mcqs.e: The Bahmani kingdom extended only up to the Krishna, not to Madurai.

mcqs.q: What is the region between the Krishna and the Tungabhadra called?
mcqs.e: The Raichur Doab was the main cause of the Bahmani-Vijayanagara conflict.

mcqs.q: Into how many states did the Bahmani kingdom break up?
mcqs.e: Berar, Bijapur, Ahmadnagar, Bidar and Golconda.

mcqs.q: Which dynasty ruled Berar?
mcqs.e: Fathullah Imad-ul-Mulk was its first ruler.

mcqs.q: Which dynasty ruled Bijapur?
mcqs.e: The Adil Shahis built the Gol Gumbaz.

mcqs.q: Which dynasty ruled Ahmadnagar?
mcqs.e: Ahmadnagar was ruled by the Nizam Shahis.

mcqs.q: Which dynasty ruled Bidar?
mcqs.e: The Barid Shahis ruled Bidar.

mcqs.q: Which dynasty ruled Golconda?
mcqs.e: The Qutb Shahis built the Charminar in Hyderabad.

mcqs.q: Which dynasty built the Gol Gumbaz of Bijapur?
mcqs.e: It is among the largest domes in the world.

mcqs.q: Where is the Gol Gumbaz located?
mcqs.e: The Gol Gumbaz is the tomb of Muhammad Adil Shah.

mcqs.q: Which dynasty built the Charminar of Hyderabad?
mcqs.e: Built in 1591 by Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah.

mcqs.q: On his father's side, Babur was a descendant of whom?
mcqs.e: Babur descended from Timur on his father's side and from Genghis Khan on his mother's side.

mcqs.q: On his mother's side, Babur was a descendant of which great conqueror?
mcqs.e: Through his mother, who was of Mongol descent.

mcqs.q: At the age of 12, Babur ascended the throne of which kingdom?
mcqs.e: Fergana lies in present-day Uzbekistan.

mcqs.q: When did Babur capture Kabul?
mcqs.e: Kabul is in Afghanistan.

mcqs.q: In which year did Babur assume the title of 'Padshah'?
mcqs.e: He took this title after establishing himself at Kabul.

mcqs.q: Who wrote 'Tarikh-i-Rashidi'?
mcqs.e: He was Babur's cousin; the work covers Central Asia and early Mughal history.

mcqs.q: Who wrote 'Tabaqat-i-Nasiri'?
mcqs.e: Minhaj-us-Siraj was a historian of the Iltutmish-Nasiruddin Mahmud era.

mcqs.q: Who wrote 'Fatawa-i-Jahandari'?
mcqs.e: Barani also wrote the Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi.

mcqs.q: Who was the first to use gunpowder (artillery) on a large scale in India?
mcqs.e: Babur used artillery in the First Battle of Panipat.

mcqs.q: What did Babur's 'Tulughma' method of warfare involve?
o: Encircling the enemy from both flanks
mcqs.e: In tulughma, army units encircled and attacked the enemy from the left and right flanks.

mcqs.q: Who was the last ruler of the Delhi Sultanate?
mcqs.e: He was killed at Panipat in 1526, ending the Sultanate.

mcqs.q: Who is considered prominent among those who invited Babur to India?
mcqs.e: Daulat Khan Lodi was the governor of Punjab; Alam Khan Lodi also invited Babur.

mcqs.q: In which language was Babur's autobiography 'Tuzuk-i-Baburi' written?
mcqs.e: Its Persian translation is known as the 'Baburnama'.

mcqs.q: Who translated the Tuzuk-i-Baburi into Persian (Baburnama)?
mcqs.e: Khan-i-Khanan was one of Akbar's Navaratnas.

mcqs.q: When was the First Battle of Panipat fought?
mcqs.e: Sequence: Panipat 1526, Khanwa 1527, Chanderi 1528, Ghaghra 1529, Babur's death 1530.

mcqs.q: The Battle of Khanwa was fought between Babur and whom?
mcqs.e: Rana Sanga was a Sisodia Rajput ruler of Mewar.

mcqs.q: When was the Battle of Khanwa fought?
mcqs.e: Babur was victorious.

mcqs.q: Whom did Babur defeat in the Battle of Chanderi (1528)?
mcqs.e: Medini Rai, a Rajput chief of Malwa, was defeated.

mcqs.q: Whom did Babur defeat in the Battle of Ghaghra (1529)?
mcqs.e: Babur died in 1530, a year after Ghaghra.

mcqs.q: In which battle did Rana Sanga defeat Ibrahim Lodi?
mcqs.e: Rana Sanga defeated Ibrahim Lodi at Khatoli.

mcqs.q: When did Babur die?
mcqs.e: He was first buried at the Aram Bagh in Agra.

mcqs.q: Where was Babur first buried, a place regarded as the first Mughal garden?
mcqs.e: His remains were later taken to Kabul and reburied.

mcqs.q: Where was Babur finally buried, in accordance with his wishes?
mcqs.e: His remains were moved from Agra to Bagh-e-Babur in Kabul.

mcqs.q: How did Qutbuddin Aibak die?
o: By falling from his horse while playing chaugan (polo)
mcqs.e: He ruled from 1206 to 1210.

mcqs.q: The construction of the Qutub Minar was begun in the name of which saint?
mcqs.e: Aibak began it and Iltutmish completed it.

mcqs.q: Where is the 'Adhai Din Ka Jhonpra' located?
mcqs.e: It was built by Qutbuddin Aibak.

mcqs.q: Which of the following was NOT a son of Babur?
mcqs.e: Babur's sons: Humayun, Kamran, Askari and Hindal; Shuja was Shah Jahan's son.

mcqs.q: Humayun divided the empire among his brothers because...
o: in Timurid-Mongol tradition the kingdom was shared among sons
mcqs.e: Kamran received Kabul, Kandahar and Punjab.

mcqs.q: When was the Battle of Chausa fought?
mcqs.e: Sher Shah defeated Humayun at Chausa.

mcqs.q: When was the Battle of Bilgram (Kannauj) fought?
mcqs.e: Humayun was again defeated by Sher Shah.

mcqs.q: The battles of Chausa and Kannauj were fought between Humayun and whom?
mcqs.e: Sher Shah was an Afghan whose father was a jagirdar in Bihar.

mcqs.q: After his defeat, Humayun took refuge with the ruler of which Iranian dynasty?
mcqs.e: Akbar was born (1542) while Humayun was in flight.

mcqs.q: In Sher Shah Suri's administration, which unit was equivalent to the Mughal 'sarkar'?
mcqs.e: The Mughal sarkar was called shiq under Sher Shah.

mcqs.q: What was the largest administrative unit (province) under Sher Shah?
mcqs.e: The pargana was a sub-district unit.

mcqs.q: In Sher Shah's administration, who was the treasurer at the pargana level?
mcqs.e: The shiqdar was the officer in charge of a shiq.

mcqs.q: Who was the village headman during Sher Shah's time?
mcqs.e: The qazi was a judicial officer.

mcqs.q: Akbar was inspired by and adopted whose administrative system?
mcqs.e: Akbar adopted and further developed Sher Shah's system.

mcqs.q: Where did Sher Shah Suri die?
mcqs.e: He died in 1545 in a gunpowder explosion during the siege of Kalinjar.

mcqs.q: Where is the tomb of Sher Shah Suri located?
mcqs.e: Akbar's tomb is at Sikandra, Agra.

mcqs.q: When did Sher Shah die?
mcqs.e: Humayun returned in 1555.

mcqs.q: When did Humayun defeat the Surs and recapture Delhi?
mcqs.e: He died the next year, in 1556.

mcqs.q: How did Humayun die?
o: By falling from the stairs of his library
mcqs.e: He fell from the stairs of the Sher Mandal in Purana Qila, Delhi.

mcqs.q: At what age did Akbar ascend the throne?
mcqs.e: Bairam Khan acted as his regent.

mcqs.q: Who led Akbar's army in the Second Battle of Panipat (1556)?
mcqs.e: The opposing Afghan army was led by Hemu (Hemchandra Vikramaditya).

mcqs.q: Who led the Afghan army in the Second Battle of Panipat?
mcqs.e: Hemu's army fled after an arrow struck him in the eye.

mcqs.q: What was the period of Akbar's reign?
mcqs.e: His long reign rested on an efficient administrative system.

mcqs.q: Who adopted the policy of 'Sulh-i-Kul'?
mcqs.e: Sulh-i-Kul means 'peace with all'.

mcqs.q: What was Akbar's full name?
mcqs.e: Babur's name was Zahiruddin Muhammad Babur.

mcqs.q: What was Babur's original name?
mcqs.e: Zahir for Babur, Jalal for Akbar.

mcqs.q: Who wrote the 'Humayun-nama'?
mcqs.e: She was Humayun's half-sister.

mcqs.q: In which year did Akbar introduce the Mansabdari system?
mcqs.e: Mansab means rank or position.

mcqs.q: On what basis was a mansab determined?
mcqs.e: Zat denoted personal rank; sawar denoted the number of cavalrymen.

mcqs.q: What were mansabdars who received jagirs called during the Mughal period?
mcqs.e: Lower-ranking mansabdars were often paid in cash.

mcqs.q: Which new faith did Akbar found, which Birbal was the only prominent Hindu to adopt?
mcqs.e: It was founded in 1582.

mcqs.q: When was Din-i-Ilahi founded?
mcqs.e: Birbal was the only prominent Hindu to adopt it.

mcqs.q: What was Akbar's translation department called?
mcqs.e: Maktab Khana = house of translation.

mcqs.q: What was Akbar's 'Ibadat Khana'?
mcqs.e: It was built at Fatehpur Sikri in 1575.

mcqs.q: The 'Dahsala' system was introduced by whom?
o: Akbar (with Todar Mal playing the key role)
mcqs.e: Raja Todar Mal was the finance minister.

mcqs.q: What is another name for the Dahsala system?
mcqs.e: It was based on the average of the previous 10 years.

mcqs.q: In approximately which year was the Dahsala system introduced?
mcqs.e: It was a land revenue system.

mcqs.q: Under Dahsala, the most fertile land cultivated every year was called?
mcqs.e: The other categories were Parauti, Chachar and Banjar.

mcqs.q: What was Parauti land?
mcqs.e: It was left fallow to regain fertility.

mcqs.q: For how many years was Chachar land left fallow?
mcqs.e: Banjar land was uncultivated for 5 years or more.

mcqs.q: In the Mughal administration, who headed the military department (recruitment, inspection, dagh-chehra)?
mcqs.e: The Mir Bakhshi was the head of the military department and the paymaster.

mcqs.q: Who headed the religious department at the Mughal court?
mcqs.e: The Sadr-us-Sudur looked after religious affairs and charitable grants.

mcqs.q: Who supervised the royal karkhanas (workshops)?
mcqs.e: He was also responsible for managing the royal household.

mcqs.q: The Diwan-i-Insha department dealt with what?
mcqs.e: It drafted royal orders and state correspondence.

mcqs.q: Who was the head of a Mughal suba (province)?
mcqs.e: The subedar was responsible for law and order.

mcqs.q: Who headed the revenue department in a Mughal suba?
mcqs.e: He was the head of provincial revenue and finance.

mcqs.q: What was the function of the 'Dak Chowki' in the Mughal period?
mcqs.e: It was the postal relay system.

mcqs.q: Abul Fazl was the court historian of which ruler?
mcqs.e: He wrote the Akbarnama.

mcqs.q: How many volumes does the Akbarnama have in all?
mcqs.e: Volume 1: ancestors; Volume 2: reign; Volume 3: Ain-i-Akbari.

mcqs.q: Which volume of the Akbarnama describes Akbar's administration, army, revenue and the geography of the empire?
mcqs.e: The Ain-i-Akbari is the third volume of the Akbarnama.

mcqs.q: What is described in the first volume of the Akbarnama?
mcqs.e: The second volume covers his reign.

mcqs.q: Who is regarded as the last powerful ruler in Mughal history?
mcqs.e: Bahadur Shah Zafar was the last Mughal emperor but not a powerful one.

mcqs.q: What was the period of Shah Jahan's reign?
mcqs.e: He wanted his eldest son Dara Shikoh to succeed him.

mcqs.q: What was the period of Aurangzeb's reign?
mcqs.e: He took the title 'Alamgir'.

mcqs.q: In which battles of 1658 did Aurangzeb defeat the imperial forces of Dara Shikoh's side?
mcqs.e: Both battles were fought in 1658 during the war of succession.

mcqs.q: Which title did Aurangzeb assume?
mcqs.e: Alamgir means 'conqueror of the world'.

mcqs.q: The ninth Sikh Guru, Tegh Bahadur, was executed on whose orders?
mcqs.e: He was executed in Delhi in 1675.

mcqs.q: When did Aurangzeb annex Bijapur to the Mughal Empire?
mcqs.e: Bijapur and Golconda were the last surviving Deccan sultanates.

mcqs.q: When did Aurangzeb annex Golconda?
mcqs.e: Ahmadnagar, Bidar and Berar had already come under the Mughals earlier.

mcqs.q: Lachit Borphukan was the commander of which kingdom?
mcqs.e: He defeated the Mughals in the Battle of Saraighat.

mcqs.q: When and on which river was the Battle of Saraighat fought?
mcqs.e: The Mughal army was led by Raja Ram Singh I.

mcqs.q: Who led the Mughal army in the Battle of Saraighat?
mcqs.e: Aurangzeb had sent him against the Ahoms.

mcqs.q: The NDA gold medal for the best passing-out cadet is named after whom?
mcqs.e: It is called the Lachit Borphukan Gold Medal.

mcqs.q: Who was the first Nawab (subedar) of Awadh?
mcqs.e: Awadh became virtually independent around 1722.

mcqs.q: Who was the first Nizam of Hyderabad?
mcqs.e: He founded the Asaf Jahi dynasty.

mcqs.q: Who was the first Nawab of Bengal?
mcqs.e: He rose from Diwan to Nawab.

mcqs.q: Who invaded India in 1739?
mcqs.e: Nadir Shah was the ruler of Persia.

mcqs.q: Who was the Mughal emperor at the time of Nadir Shah's invasion?
mcqs.e: He was defeated in the Battle of Karnal.

mcqs.q: Which famous Mughal throne did Nadir Shah carry away?
mcqs.e: The Peacock Throne was built by Shah Jahan; Nadir Shah also took the Kohinoor.

mcqs.q: In which battle did Nadir Shah defeat the Mughal army?
mcqs.e: This was followed by a massacre and plunder in Delhi.

mcqs.q: Which feature distinguished Mughal architecture from the earlier temple style?
o: Extensive use of arches and domes
mcqs.e: Arches, domes and minarets were prominent in Mughal architecture.

mcqs.q: What was a 'sarai'?
mcqs.e: Sher Shah built sarais along the road later called the Grand Trunk Road.

mcqs.q: Which building in the royal palace was used for private audiences?
mcqs.e: The Diwan-i-Aam was the hall of public audience.

mcqs.q: Which city did Akbar develop as a planned capital?
mcqs.e: Work on it began in 1571.

mcqs.q: Fatehpur Sikri was built in honour of the blessings of which saint?
mcqs.e: Jahangir (Salim) was born with his blessings.

mcqs.q: The Buland Darwaza was built to commemorate what?
mcqs.e: Built c. 1575 at Fatehpur Sikri.

mcqs.q: Where is the tomb of Salim Chishti located?
mcqs.e: Akbar's tomb is at Sikandra (Agra).

mcqs.q: Where is Akbar's tomb located?
mcqs.e: Sher Shah's tomb is at Sasaram (Bihar).

mcqs.q: The Jahangiri Mahal is built of which stone?
mcqs.e: It stands in Agra Fort; the Panch Mahal is also of red sandstone.

mcqs.q: Who built the Panch Mahal and which style influenced it?
mcqs.e: It is located at Fatehpur Sikri.

mcqs.q: When was the construction of the Taj Mahal completed?
mcqs.e: Work began after Mumtaz Mahal's death in 1631; it is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

mcqs.q: Who built the Taj Mahal?
mcqs.e: In memory of Mumtaz Mahal.

mcqs.q: What is the technique of inlaying precious stones in marble called?
mcqs.e: It is prominent in the Taj Mahal.

mcqs.q: Which building has an early example of pietra dura (inlaid marble work)?
mcqs.e: It is also called the 'Baby Taj'.

mcqs.q: Who built the tomb of Itmad-ud-Daulah?
mcqs.e: She built it in Agra in memory of her father.

mcqs.q: Ustad Ahmad Lahori is regarded as the chief architect of which building?
mcqs.e: He was the chief architect of the Taj Mahal, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

mcqs.q: Which of the following buildings is built in the charbagh style?
mcqs.e: The Mughals popularised the charbagh garden layout.

mcqs.q: Who commissioned Humayun's Tomb?
